story: Petersburg Assembly broadens its temporary data center moratorium (Ordinance 2026-24) to cover all data centers, with the final vote set for November 30th, plus Fairbanks North Star Borough context and an AIDEA runner-up

claims.claim: The Petersburg Borough Assembly voted 5-2 to broaden the proposed data center moratorium so it would apply to all data center development.
claims.verbatim: Last week, assembly members voted 5–2 to broaden the proposed moratorium, so it would apply to “all” data center development.
claims.notes: The vote was at the November 16th regular meeting. Independently corroborated by the Petersburg Pilot (November 19th): 'The Assembly approved Member Jeff Meucci's amendment 5-2'. The verbatim keeps the page's own en dash and curly quotes.

claims.claim: Assembly Member Jeff Meucci proposed the amendment that broadened the moratorium.
claims.verbatim: Assembly Member Jeff Meucci pitched the amendment.
claims.notes: Corroborated by the Petersburg Pilot, which calls it 'Member Jeff Meucci's amendment'.

claims.claim: Mayor Bob Lynn and Vice Mayor Jeigh Stanton Gregor voted against the broadening amendment.
claims.verbatim: The Assembly approved the amendment, with Lynn and Stanton Gregor voting against.
claims.notes: Corroborated by the Petersburg Pilot lede, which names Mayor Bob Lynn and Vice Mayor Jeigh Stanton Gregor as opposed. The ordinance signature line names the mayor as Robert Lynn.

claims.claim: The amended Ordinance 2026-24 passed its second reading unanimously, 7-0.
claims.verbatim: The overall ordinance passed unanimously, 7–0, in its second reading.
claims.notes: Independently corroborated by the Petersburg Pilot: 'passing Ordinance 2026-24 on second reading 7-0'. No official minutes were fetched, so this rests on two independent news reports.

claims.claim: The moratorium needs one more round of Assembly approval before it can take effect.
claims.verbatim: The measure will require one more round of Assembly approval before it can take effect.
claims.notes: Consistent with the three-reading process the November 16th agenda describes ('If approved in three readings').

claims.claim: The Assembly is set to take up the moratorium again on November 30th at 6 p.m.
claims.verbatim: at the next assembly meeting, which happens Nov. 30 at 6:00 p.m.
claims.notes: This is a future event, so it is a schedule, not an outcome. The Petersburg Pilot calls it a special Assembly meeting at 6 p.m. November 30th where 'The final vote is expected'. The borough's CivicClerk event list was not fetched.

claims.claim: The November 30th meeting will include another public hearing on the amended moratorium.
claims.verbatim: There will be another public hearing for the proposed moratorium, as amended, during that meeting.
claims.notes: Corroborated by the Petersburg Pilot (see C08).

claims.claim: The additional public hearing was recommended by the borough attorney, according to the Petersburg Pilot.
claims.verbatim: along with – at the recommendation of the borough attorney -- an additional public hearing
claims.notes: Single source. The sentence is cut off at the paywall, and the fragment is verbatim as returned, page dashes included. Attribute it to the Pilot.

claims.claim: The Petersburg Pilot reported that the amendment closes the opening left for Mazzella's 2-megawatt data center.
claims.verbatim: Amendment closes the opening left for Mazzella’s 2-megawatt data center
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to the Petersburg Pilot, the amendment closes the opening
claims.notes: This is the Pilot's subhead and its framing. The effect on Mazzella's project is the Pilot's interpretation, not a ruling. The 2-megawatt figure matches the transformer Mazzella owns (C43).

claims.claim: As amended, the moratorium applies whether a project runs on or off the local grid and whatever cooling system it uses.
claims.verbatim: regardless of whether a project runs off or on the local power grid, or what kind of cooling system it uses.
claims.suggested_phrasing: as amended, the moratorium would apply
claims.notes: KFSK says staff are still revising the text ('as Borough staff work on a revised version'), so the amended wording isn't published. The fetched primary PDF is the introduced version with the narrower C.1 to C.3 conditions.

claims.claim: Meucci argued for a full moratorium on any additional data center building permits.
claims.verbatim: we’re going to take a real moratorium, and stop any kind of additional building permits for any kind of data center
claims.notes: The quote is verbatim on the page. The attribution to Meucci rests on the fetch's paraphrase ('Assembly Member Jeff Meucci proposed the amendment, saying we're going to take a real moratorium'). The attribution sentence itself wasn't retrieved verbatim. Quote only the fragment shown.

claims.claim: Utility Director Steve Harbour helped write the ordinance.
claims.verbatim: Utility Director Steve Harbour, who helped author the ordinance,
claims.notes: The agenda (C18 source) confirms Harbour as Utility Director. The agenda spells his first name 'Stephan' in item 15E. KFSK uses 'Steve'.

claims.claim: Harbour said nobody wants generators running around the clock and that this is the purpose of the ordinance.
claims.verbatim: But I do know none of us wants generators running 24/7, and that’s the purpose of this ordinance
claims.notes: The quote is verbatim. The attribution to Harbour is per the page paraphrase and the adjacent attribution sentence (C12).

claims.claim: Assembly Member James Valentine said the moratorium gives the borough time and that he would vote yes.
claims.verbatim: “I like it. It gives us time, and I will be voting yes,” said Assembly Member James Valentine.
claims.notes: The attribution is in the same sentence.

claims.claim: Assembly Member Bob Martin said diesel generation was the biggest open door.
claims.verbatim: But I still think the biggest open door here, as Member Meucci referenced, is diesel generation.
claims.notes: The attribution comes from the preceding sentence, "'This has gotten tougher and tougher as time goes on,' said Assembly Member Bob Martin." The fetch tool reported that the diesel remark continues his quote. Martin voted with the majority on the amendment, since only Lynn and Stanton Gregor voted no.

claims.claim: Stanton Gregor called the amendment a solution in search of a problem.
claims.value: a solution in search of a problem
claims.verbatim: I think the amendment is a solution in search of a problem.
claims.notes: The quote is verbatim. The attribution to Vice Mayor Jeigh Stanton Gregor rests on the page paraphrase. KFSK on September 28th also attributes 'feels like a solution in search of a problem' to him about the September proposal, so it's a phrase he has used before.

claims.claim: Mayor Bob Lynn is board chair of the Southeast Alaska Power Agency, the wholesale hydropower supplier.
claims.verbatim: He is the board chair of Southeast Alaska Power Agency, the wholesale hydropower supplier
claims.suggested_phrasing: according to KFSK, Lynn chairs the SEAPA board
claims.notes: The verbatim's 'He' refers to Lynn per the surrounding paraphrase. No SEAPA page was fetched. The November 16th agenda (item 15E) shows Lynn applying for Petersburg's 2027 SEAPA board seat. Don't imply a conflict of interest, because KFSK doesn't allege one.

claims.claim: Ordinance 2026-24 passed its first reading by a vote of 5-1.
claims.verbatim: Ordinance #2026-24 passed its first reading by a vote of 5-1.
claims.notes: WebFetched this run, with the PDF bytes read page by page (page 3, item 14A). The PDF metadata creation date is November 12th, for the meeting on Monday, November 16th. KFSK on November 11th corroborates the 5-1 vote. The first reading was on November 2nd.

claims.claim: At the November 2nd first reading, Meucci's amendment to cover all data centers failed in a 3-3 tie.
claims.verbatim: Meucci’s amendment failed in a 3–3 tie vote.
claims.notes: Background, since the source predates the November 14th to 24th window. The page also says 'The Petersburg Borough Assembly on Nov. 2 considered a potential moratorium'. Meucci then voted no on advancing the narrower version, per the same article.

claims.claim: Member Donna Marsh seconded Meucci's November 2nd amendment.
claims.verbatim: Meucci motioned during the assembly meeting, seconded by Member Marsh.
claims.notes: The fetch tool flagged the sentence as truncated. The first name Donna is from the same article's paraphrase ('Assembly Member Donna Marsh'). Marsh's own quote in the November 23rd story wasn't used (banned word).

claims.claim: Assembly Member Scott Newman was excused from the November 2nd meeting, when the moratorium advanced 5-1.
claims.verbatim: Assembly Member Scott Newman was excused from the meeting.
claims.notes: The same page says 'Members ultimately voted 5–1 to move the proposed moratorium forward to a second round of consideration.' That explains six votes on November 2nd and seven on November 16th.

claims.claim: There were no data centers in Petersburg as of KFSK's November 11th report.
claims.verbatim: There are currently no data centers in Petersburg, but they’re discussed regularly at assembly meetings.
claims.suggested_phrasing: as of mid-November, Petersburg had no data centers, according to KFSK
claims.notes: Date-bound. Keep the 'as of' framing.

claims.claim: Harbour told the Assembly a generator ban was needed because a generator-powered data center was not out of the realm of possibilities.
claims.value: not out of the realm of possibilities
claims.verbatim: this ordinance needs to pass banning generators because it’s not out of the realm of possibilities
claims.suggested_phrasing: Harbour urged a generator ban, telling the Assembly it was 'not out of the realm of possibilities'
claims.notes: The fragment is verbatim but truncated by the fetch tool. The attribution rests on the page paraphrase ('Utility Director Steve Harbour urged the Assembly to pass a version that bans generator-powered data centers'). Background, November 2nd meeting.

claims.claim: KFSK reported that the moratorium as written would apply where the borough has platting authority.
claims.verbatim: As written, the moratorium would apply where the Borough has platting authority.
claims.notes: The primary text (Section 3.A) says it 'applies wherever the Borough has authority to issue the permit or approval and does not create or expand building-code enforcement authority outside an authorized service area'. Prefer the primary wording. 'Platting authority' is KFSK's gloss.

claims.claim: Ordinance 2026-24 as introduced was titled as a temporary moratorium on borough permits for certain data center development.
claims.verbatim: AN ORDINANCE ESTABLISHING A TEMPORARY MORATORIUM ON ISSUANCE OF BOROUGH PERMITS FOR CERTAIN DATA CENTER DEVELOPMENT
claims.notes: WebFetched this run, with the PDF pages read directly (5 pages). It matches the showrunner's local extraction. The document itself is undated. The October 29th date is the showrunner-reported PDF creation date, not independently checked, and the upload folder is 2026/11. This is the INTRODUCED text. The November 16th amendment removed 'certain' in substance, and the revised text isn't yet published.

claims.claim: The ordinance defines a data center to include facilities whose principal use is artificial intelligence computing.
claims.verbatim: whose principal use is housing and operating computer servers and associated equipment for data processing, storage, hosting, artificial intelligence computing, or digital asset computing.
claims.notes: Section 3.B.1, page 2. The definition excludes accessory server rooms and network closets.

claims.claim: Under the ordinance, current grid capacity is the capacity Petersburg Municipal Power & Light determines in writing is available to the site.
claims.verbatim: The maximum electrical capacity that PMPL determines in writing is presently available and deliverable to the data center site
claims.notes: Section 3.B.3. Capacity that depends on future upgrades is excluded. PMPL is defined in B.4 as Petersburg Municipal Power & Light.

claims.claim: The ordinance requires a qualifying closed-loop cooling system to keep 100 percent of its coolant and refrigerant circuits contained.
claims.verbatim: A cooling system in which One Hundred Percent (100%) of the liquid coolant and refrigerant circuits remain contained and recirculate during all operations
claims.notes: Section 3.B.5. Evaporative cooling towers are barred and dry air heat rejection is permitted.

claims.claim: As introduced, the ordinance barred permits for a data center whose load PMPL's current grid capacity couldn't fully supply or that would breach a SEAPA limitation.
claims.verbatim: would not be fully supplied by PMPL’s current grid capacity or would exceed or violate an applicable restriction ... including without limitation the Southeast Alaska Power Agency (SEAPA).
claims.suggested_phrasing: as introduced, the ordinance would have barred
claims.notes: Section 3.C.1. The ellipsis marks omitted words. The November 16th amendment broadened the bar to all data centers, so present this as the original, narrower version.

claims.claim: As introduced, the ordinance barred permits for a data center relying on diesel, natural gas or other generators for its normal operating load.
claims.verbatim: The data center proposal relies on diesel, natural gas, fuel or other generators to provide its normal operating electrical load
claims.notes: Section 3.C.2. It covers primary, continuous, temporary, supplemental or peak-shaving power.

claims.claim: As introduced, the ordinance barred permits for a data center if any part of its cooling system was not fully self-contained and closed-loop.
claims.verbatim: Any part of the data center’s cooling system fails to meet the fully self-contained, closed-loop requirements of subsection B.5.
claims.notes: Section 3.C.3, page 3.

claims.claim: The ordinance permits backup generators during an actual grid outage or a curtailment directed by PMPL.
claims.verbatim: Subsection C.2 does not prohibit use of back-up generators to maintain business continuity, protect equipment, or provide life safety during an actual interruption of grid power serving the data center or during a curtailment directed by PMPL.
claims.notes: Section 3.D.1 (39 words). Whether this survives the all-data-center amendment is unknown until the revised text is published.

claims.claim: The ordinance requires cooling plans certified by an Alaska-licensed professional engineer.
claims.verbatim: The applicant shall submit cooling plans and a certification of compliance, prepared by an Alaska-licensed professional engineer qualified to evaluate the proposed system
claims.notes: Section 3.E.3.

claims.claim: The Borough Manager must return findings and recommendations on data centers to the Assembly on or before June 21st, 2027.
claims.verbatim: return to the Assembly with findings and recommendations on or before June 21, 2027.
claims.notes: Section 4, page 4. The year is kept because it differs from the current year.

claims.claim: The moratorium expires automatically at 11:59 p.m. Alaska time on September 30th, 2027, unless the Assembly extends or repeals it.
claims.verbatim: The moratorium shall expire automatically, with no further action of the Assembly required, at 11:59 p.m., Alaska time, on the 30th day of September, 2027
claims.notes: Section 6 (the page has a double space after 'moratorium'). The November 16th agenda also says 'through September 30, 2027'.

claims.claim: The review covers authority to apply future data center rules throughout the borough, excluding the City of Kupreanof.
claims.verbatim: Authority and procedures needed to apply future data center regulations throughout the Borough, excluding the City of Kupreanof.
claims.notes: Section 4.H. This is a review topic, not a geographic limit on the moratorium itself. Don't write that the moratorium excludes Kupreanof.

claims.claim: The ordinance does not revoke a valid permit issued before its adoption.
claims.verbatim: This ordinance does not revoke a valid permit issued before its adoption.
claims.notes: Section 3.E.6.

claims.claim: The ordinance and its moratorium take effect upon adoption.
claims.verbatim: This ordinance, and the moratorium adopted hereunder, are effective upon adoption.
claims.notes: Section 6.

claims.claim: The moratorium applies even to applications pending on the date of adoption.
claims.verbatim: applies regardless of whether an application is pending upon the date of adoption of this ordinance.
claims.notes: Section 3.A.

claims.claim: Ordinance 2026-25 would authorize up to $3,315,000 in electric utility revenue bonds for the Scow Bay Standby Generation Project.
claims.verbatim: Ordinance #2026-25 will authorize the issuance of up to $3,315,000 in Electric Utility revenue bonds to finance improvements to the Scow Bay Standby Generation Project
claims.notes: Item 15A, first reading on November 16th. The Petersburg Pilot (November 19th) gives $3.315 million. This is the borough's own standby generation, so contrast it with the data center generator bar with care.

claims.claim: Voters ratified the Scow Bay generation borrowing at an election on October 6th.
claims.verbatim: Ratified by the Borough’s Voters At An Election Held Therein On October 6, 2026
claims.notes: Item 15A title, page 3.

claims.claim: Borough staff recommended a special Assembly meeting on November 30th for the second reading of the bond ordinance.
claims.verbatim: Staff recommends calling a special Assembly meeting on November 30, 2026, to allow for the second reading of Bond Authorization Ordinance #2026-25.
claims.notes: Item 15G, verified from the showrunner's extraction. Page 5 of the fetched PDF wasn't visually rendered, since only pages 1 to 3 were read. Whether the meeting was called is from KFSK and the Pilot (C06).

claims.claim: Developer Andrew Mazzella owns the 2-megawatt transformer that powered the former Ocean Beauty cannery.
claims.verbatim: Mazzella also owns the 2-megawatt transformer that powered the cannery before the plant ceased operations in 2016.
claims.notes: Background from May. The same page says 'Mazzella bought the former Ocean Beauty properties on Petersburg’s downtown waterfront in 2024.'

claims.claim: Petersburg runs on hydropower.
claims.verbatim: Petersburg runs on hydropower.
claims.notes: The November 23rd KFSK story calls SEAPA 'the wholesale hydropower supplier'.

claims.claim: Petersburg buys most of its power from the Southeast Alaska Power Agency, which also supplies Wrangell and Ketchikan.
claims.verbatim: buys most of it from Southeast Alaska Power Agency, a regional supplier that sends power to Petersburg, Wrangell and Ketchikan.
claims.notes: The fetch tool joined two truncated fragments of the same passage. Petersburg also has its own plant south of town.

claims.claim: Petersburg's power department estimated in May that the waterfront data center could generate 1 to 2 million dollars in revenue a year.
claims.verbatim: they estimate it’d generate $1–2 million in revenue each year
claims.suggested_phrasing: the utility estimated in May that it could generate
claims.notes: This is a projection made for the earlier Greensparc version of the project, which did not finalize (C48).

claims.claim: The power department said in May the data center would lower Petersburg's projected annual rate increases from about 4 percent to about 2 percent.
claims.verbatim: However, according to the department, the data center would lower that figure to about 2%.
claims.notes: The preceding sentence says rates 'are projected to increase annually by about 4%'. This CORRECTS the brief, which said 5 percent falling to 0. The 5 percent appears only in a photo caption for 2028, and no 0 figure was found. It's a projection.

claims.claim: Mazzella Alaska's deal with Silicon Valley data center vendor Greensparc did not finalize.
claims.verbatim: Its private business deal with a Silicon Valley-based data center vendor, Greensparc, did not finalize.
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: As of late September, Mazzella Alaska said it was still pursuing a small-scale data center.
claims.verbatim: Mazzella Alaska confirmed it is still pursuing a small-scale data center aligned with the initially announced plan.
claims.suggested_phrasing: as of September, the company said it was still pursuing
claims.notes: Date-bound. Its current status after the November 16th amendment wasn't verified.

claims.claim: On September 21st, an earlier year-long data center moratorium proposal deadlocked 3-3 in the Petersburg Assembly.
claims.verbatim: landing in a tie 3–3 vote after discussing it for 30 minutes.
claims.notes: The same page has 'The Petersburg Borough Assembly on Sept. 21 considered pursuing a temporary moratorium regarding data centers' and 'a year-long freeze on issuing applications or permits for data centers'.

claims.claim: On October 5th the Assembly directed staff to draft an ordinance for a nine-month moratorium on certain data center projects.
claims.verbatim: to draft an ordinance for a nine-month moratorium on certain data center projects.
claims.notes: The page also says 'The Petersburg Borough Assembly approved two different data center-related measures on Oct. 5.' Sanity check on the numbers: the drafted ordinance's September 30th, 2027 expiry runs longer than nine months from a November or December adoption, so don't present nine months as the final length.

claims.claim: When Petersburg became a borough in 2013, it incorporated 3,829 square miles of land.
claims.verbatim: When Petersburg became a borough in 2013, it incorporated 3,829 square miles of land
claims.notes: Background.

claims.claim: The Fairbanks North Star Borough Planning Commission extended the mayor's proposed 12-month data center moratorium to 18 months.
claims.verbatim: extending the mayor’s proposed 12-month timeframe to 18.
claims.notes: The page timestamp is 'Published: Nov. 16, 2026 at 3:34 PM AKST', although the URL path says 11/17. The byline is Alex Bengel. The proposal is Mayor Grier Hopkins' moratorium on large-scale data center permits. It's single-sourced (news report of a commission action), and no primary FNSB document was fetched.

claims.claim: The commission also lengthened the administration's research timeline from six months to 10.
claims.verbatim: The commission also increased the timeline for the administration ... from six months to 10.
claims.notes: The ellipsis marks words omitted by the fetch tool.

claims.claim: Mayor Hopkins said the Fairbanks North Star Borough Assembly vote will likely take place on January 14th.
claims.verbatim: with Hopkins saying a vote will likely take place on Jan. 14.
claims.suggested_phrasing: a vote is expected around January 14th, Hopkins said
claims.notes: This is a projection. The year is 2027 but is implied, so write 'January 14th' carefully, because it isn't this year. Consider 'January 14th, 2027' for clarity.

claims.claim: AIDEA's November 24th board meeting went into recess.
claims.verbatim: The November 24, 2026 AIDEA Board Meeting is now in recess and will resume at 10:00 AM on Friday, November 27, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: The page is undated. The date_of_source is inferred from the notice, and the page was fetched November 25th. The fetch also lists the November 24th session as a continuation of the November 19th meeting, but that wasn't verbatim. Nothing on the page says what is on the agenda.

claims.claim: The AIDEA board meeting is set to resume on Friday, November 27th.
claims.verbatim: The November 24, 2026 AIDEA Board Meeting is now in recess and will resume at 10:00 AM on Friday, November 27, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: The page says dates and times are subject to change.

claims.claim: The resumed AIDEA session is scheduled for 10 a.m.
claims.verbatim: The November 24, 2026 AIDEA Board Meeting is now in recess and will resume at 10:00 AM on Friday, November 27, 2026.
claims.source_outlet: Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority
claims.notes: This is the same sentence as C56 and C57. It's a thin runner-up with no substantive item verified.

killed.why: The quote is verbatim on the KFSK November 23rd page, but who said it was never retrieved, and a named-person attribution can't rest on the brief.

killed.claim: Stanton Gregor said his biggest concern was 'insulating ourselves from off-grid threats to our community'
killed.why: The quote is verbatim, but the attribution sentence wasn't retrieved.

killed.claim: Stanton Gregor said the ordinance would 'prevent an off-grid, large-scale, multi-acre data center from cropping up in Petersburg'
killed.why: The fetch tool cut the sentence off and the speaker is 'He' with no confirmed name. The attribution is unverified.

killed.claim: Vice Mayor Stanton Gregor sponsored or proposed the original ordinance
killed.why: It appears only in fetch-tool paraphrases on the November 11th and 23rd pages, with no verbatim sentence captured. KFSK on October 16th does say he proposed the nine-month moratorium direction, but that's paraphrase too.

killed.claim: The utility projected a 5 percent rate increase in 2028 that would fall to 0 if a full 2 MW were sold
killed.why: Contradicted by the source. The KFSK May 1st article says about 4 percent annually falling to about 2 percent (see C47). The 5 percent is a photo caption for 2028, and no 0 figure exists on the page.

killed.claim: A local developer is interested in building a data center in Petersburg (KFSK November 11th)
killed.why: Only a paraphrase was captured, with no verbatim sentence. Use C43, C48 and C49 for Mazzella's interest instead.

killed.claim: The Assembly will meet only once in December after reworking its calendar (Petersburg Pilot, November 19th, story 16220)
killed.why: Only the fetch tool's summary of a paywalled lede, with no verbatim text. Agenda items 15G and 15H show the proposal, not the outcome.

killed.claim: KFSK November 16th preview details (public hearing, $800,000 hospital grant, Papke's Landing $15,000 snow removal)
killed.why: The page was fetched but only summarized, with no verbatim captured. The $800,000 and $15,000 figures do appear in the primary agenda, but they're off-story and not carried.

killed.claim: AIDEA board meeting on Friday, December 4th
killed.why: Listed only in the fetch summary with no verbatim string, and the page shows no agenda or details.
Optional source, not fetched this run. The November 30th meeting rests on KFSK and the Pilot (C06).

killed.why: It contains a banned house word, wasn't needed and wasn't verified for use.
